newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise despite profit-taking wave.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise despite profit-taking wave.

text.p: Egyptian share prices remained unaffected by profit-taking on Monday, firming in very active trade, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index rose 0.10 points to end at 234.83 points.
Volume was 74.35 million pounds ($21.89 million), with the listing of a second tranche of shares in newly privatised Upper Egypt Flour Mills accounting for 28 million.
"There are now many sellers after recent price increases," said Mohamed Magdi of Financial Brokerage Group.
The market leader was Misr Oil and Soap with shares worth 12.46 million pounds exchanging hands. But the stock ended down 0.18 pounds at 30.85.
"Many investors bought the share at a lesser price than the flotation price and they are taking profits now," broker Yasser Rashed at Triple A Securities said.
The firm was partially privatised some two months ago at a fixed price of 31 pounds per share.
"There are rumours that the holding company is the seller," a market source said.

The favourite milling companies were still dominating trade. North Cairo Flour Mills jumped 3.00 pounds to 118.00 while recently privatised West and Central Delta Flour Mills finished 1.99 pounds down at 48.45.
But the popular cement shares were the most hit by the selling spree and ended mostly lower, brokers said.

Blue-chip Suez Cement declined 0.50 pounds to 53.25 pounds. The National Bank of Egypt said on Monday it and other public-sector companies would sell about 17 percent of the company through GDRs to be listed in London.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement ended down 2.50 pounds at 61.00 pounds and Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA was also 0.75 pounds down at 49.00 pounds.
Decliners outnumbered advancers by 16 to 18, while 23 others ended unchanged.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to a new record high of 366.58 points from 363.58 on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms was steady at 159.94.
